units.same: {from} and {to} are the same step – the number stays the same!
exam.prompt.aquarium: An aquarium is {l} dm long, {b} dm wide and {h} dm high. How many litres does it hold? Write just the number.
step.aquariumVolume: The volume is length · width · height. In dm that's dm³ – and 1 dm³ is 1 litre.
step.mlIsCubicCm: 1 ml is the same as 1 cm³ – the number stays the same.
scene.balance.hint: The scale is level. Tap a weight next to the box – the same comes off both sides.
scene.balance.removed: {n} taken off both sides – the scale is still level!
scene.balance.each: Each {label} weighs as much as one of the parts: {n}.
scene.groups.hint: Tap the groups one at a time and count on: {each}, then {each} more …
scene.groups.going: Keep going – tap the next group.
scene.groups.done: All {groups} groups counted! The last number is how many there are altogether.
scene.share.hint: Share them out: tap the pile to give one at a time, or give one to each.
scene.share.done: All shared out – the same on every plate. How many did each get?
scene.round.ask: Which is nearest to {n}? Tap it.
scene.blocks.hint: Each digit is a pile of blocks. Tap a pile to see what it's worth.

word.tip.1.3.1: Read the question carefully. 'Together' and 'more' often mean plus, 'left' and 'difference' minus.
word.tip.1.3.2: 'Each' and 'twice' often mean times. 'Share equally' means divided by.
word.tip.2.11.1: What are they asking for? Write the calculation before you work it out.
word.tip.2.11.2: Split it into steps: work out one thing at a time and write what each number means.
word.tip.3.8.1: Percent of something: turn the percentage into a decimal and multiply.
word.tip.3.8.2: Call what you need to find x, and write what the text says as an equation.
step.word.difference: The difference: the bigger minus the smaller.
step.word.change: Take what it costs away from what is paid.
step.word.multiply: The same amount several times: multiply.
step.word.price: The price for several: the number times the price for one.
step.word.average: The mean: the sum divided by how many there are.
step.word.bothSides: Two long sides and two short sides: times 2.
step.word.side: A square has four equal sides: divide by 4.
step.word.perOne: How much is it for one?
step.word.minutesBetween: Turn the times into minutes and take the difference.
step.word.percentOf: The percentage of the price: turn it into a decimal and multiply.
step.word.discount: Take the discount off the price.
step.word.partOfWhole: The part divided by the whole – and as a percentage.
step.word.howManyFit: How many such packets make a kilo?
step.word.parts: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 parts: how much is one part?
step.word.totalNeeded: How many points are needed in total?
step.word.changeFactor: With 25 % VAT it's 125 % of the price: multiply by 1.25.
step.word.scaleRecipe: Scale the recipe: the amount times the number of people, divided by the recipe's people.
step.word.equation: Call the unknown x and write an equation.
step.word.collect: Simplify: x's together and numbers together.
step.word.thereAndBack: There and back is twice as far: times 2.
exam.prompt.fractionOf: How much is the fraction of the number?
exam.prompt.simplify: Simplify the fraction as far as it goes.
exam.prompt.fractionSum: Work it out. Answer with a fraction in its simplest form.
exam.prompt.toDecimal: Write the fraction as a decimal.
exam.prompt.toPercent: Write the decimal as a percentage.
exam.prompt.percentToFraction: Write the percentage as a fraction in its simplest form.
exam.prompt.convertNumberOnly: How many {to} is {value} {from}? Write just the number.
exam.prompt.hoursMinutes: How many minutes is {h} h and {m} min?
exam.prompt.calculateSimplest: Work it out. Answer with a fraction in its simplest form.
exam.prompt.round.whole: Round to the nearest whole number.
exam.prompt.speedDistance: A car drives at an average speed of {v} km/h for {t} hours. How many km does it drive?
exam.prompt.speedSpeed: A train travels {s} km in {t} hours. What was its average speed in km/h?
exam.prompt.speedTime: How many hours does it take to drive {s} km at an average speed of {v} km/h?
exam.prompt.scaleEnlarge: An insect is enlarged at scale {k}:1. In the picture it is {drawn} mm long. How many mm long is it really?
exam.prompt.scaleMapToReal: A map has the scale 1:{k}. A distance is {cm} cm on the map. How many metres is it in reality?
exam.prompt.scaleRealToMap: A map has the scale 1:{k}. A distance is {m} m in reality. How many cm is it on the map?
exam.prompt.marbles.red: A bag holds {r} red, {b} blue and {g} green marbles. You take one without looking. What is the probability that it's red?
exam.prompt.marbles.blue: A bag holds {r} red, {b} blue and {g} green marbles. You take one without looking. What is the probability that it's blue?
exam.prompt.marbles.green: A bag holds {r} red, {b} blue and {g} green marbles. You take one without looking. What is the probability that it's green?
exam.prompt.marblesTwo.red: A bag holds {r} red and {b} blue marbles. You take one without looking. What is the probability that it's red?
exam.prompt.marblesTwo.blue: A bag holds {r} red and {b} blue marbles. You take one without looking. What is the probability that it's blue?
exam.prompt.marblesTwo.green: A bag holds {r} red and {b} blue marbles. What is the probability of getting a green one?
exam.prompt.die.six: You throw an ordinary die. What is the probability of a six?
exam.prompt.die.even: You throw an ordinary die. What is the probability of an even number?
exam.prompt.die.overFour: You throw an ordinary die. What is the probability of more than 4?
exam.prompt.die.underThree: You throw an ordinary die. What is the probability of less than 3?
exam.prompt.twoHeads: You toss a coin twice. What is the probability of heads both times?
exam.prompt.twoSixes: You throw two dice. What is the probability that both show a six?
exam.prompt.sumSeven: You throw two dice. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
exam.prompt.sameNumber: You throw two dice. What is the probability that they show the same number?
exam.prompt.atLeastOneSix: You throw two dice. What is the probability that at least one shows a six?
exam.prompt.sumK: You throw two dice. What is the probability that the sum is {k}?
exam.prompt.twoDraws: A bag holds {r} red and {b} blue marbles. You take one, put it back and take another. What is the probability that both are red?
exam.prompt.coinAndDie: You toss a coin and throw a die. What is the probability of heads and a six?
exam.prompt.cube: A cube has sides of {s} cm. What is its volume in cm³?
exam.prompt.box: A box is {l} cm long, {b} cm wide and {h} cm high. What is its volume in cm³?
exam.prompt.prism: A prism has a triangle as its base. The triangle's base is {b} cm and its height {h} cm, and the prism is {len} cm long. What is its volume in cm³?
exam.prompt.cylinder: A cylinder has radius {r} cm and height {h} cm. What is its volume in cm³? Round to one decimal place.
exam.prompt.cone: A cone has radius {r} cm and height {h} cm. What is its volume in cm³? Round to one decimal place.
exam.prompt.sphere: A sphere has radius {r} cm. What is its volume in cm³? Round to one decimal place.
exam.prompt.sequenceTerm: The sequence carries on the same way. Which number is in place {n}?
exam.prompt.sequenceFormula: The sequence carries on the same way. Write an expression for the number in place n.
exam.tip.2.6.1: First split the number into as many parts as the denominator says. Then take as many parts as the numerator says.
exam.tip.2.6.2: Find the biggest number both the numerator and the denominator can be divided by, and divide both by it.
exam.tip.2.6.3: The fractions need the same denominator before you can add or subtract. Expand them first.
exam.tip.2.6.4: A fraction bar is a division sign. Percent means hundredths.
exam.tip.2.9.1: Each step between mm, cm, dm and m is 10 times. 1 km = 1000 m and 1 kg = 1000 g.
exam.tip.2.9.2: 1 l = 10 dl = 100 cl = 1000 ml. 1 dm³ is the same as 1 litre.
exam.tip.2.9.3: 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds. Half an hour is 30 minutes.
exam.tip.2.10.1: Brackets first, then multiplication and division, last addition and subtraction.
exam.tip.2.10.2: Look at the digit after the one you round to: 5 or more rounds up.
exam.tip.3.5.1: Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator. To divide by a fraction, turn it upside down and multiply.
exam.tip.3.6.1: Distance = speed · time. Speed = distance / time. Time = distance / speed.
exam.tip.3.6.2: Scale 1:500 means 1 cm on the map is 500 cm in reality.
exam.tip.3.7.2: Two things that don't affect each other: multiply the probabilities.
exam.tip.3.4.7: The volume of a prism is the area of its base times its height (length).
exam.tip.3.4.8: Cylinder: π r² h. Cone: π r² h / 3. Sphere: 4 π r³ / 3.
exam.tip.3.3.7: Find how much the numbers grow each time. The number in place n is the first number + (n − 1) times the step.
exam.tip.4.1.3: Set the two expressions equal to each other, or add the equations so one variable disappears.
step.divideNumDen: Divide both the numerator and the denominator by {n}.
step.writeSimplest: Write the fraction in its simplest form.
step.commonDenominator: Expand the fractions so both have the denominator {L}.
step.addNumerators: Add the numerators – the denominator stays the same.
step.subtractNumerators: Subtract the numerators – the denominator stays the same.
step.hundredthsArePercent: Hundredths are percent: write the number as a percentage.
step.litreIsCubicDm: 1 litre is the same as 1 dm³ – the number stays the same.
step.round.tens: Look at the ones digit: 5 or more rounds up. Write the rounded number.
step.round.hundreds: Look at the tens digit: 5 or more rounds up. Write the rounded number.
step.round.whole: Look at the tenths digit: 5 or more rounds up. Write the rounded number.
step.round.oneDecimal: Look at the hundredths digit: 5 or more rounds up. Write the rounded number.
step.round.twoDecimals: Look at the thousandths digit: 5 or more rounds up. Write the rounded number.
step.invertDivisor: Dividing by a fraction is multiplying by it turned upside down.
step.multiplyFractions: Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator.
step.distanceFormula: Distance = speed · time. Put the numbers in and work it out – set it up in a column if you need to.
step.speedFormula: Speed = distance / time. Put the numbers in.
step.timeFormula: Time = distance / speed. Put the numbers in and work it out with the bus stop.
step.scaleMultiply: 1 cm on the map is {k} cm in reality: multiply by {k}.
step.probabilityCount: Favourable outcomes divided by possible outcomes: {fav} out of {total}.
step.multiplyProbabilities: Multiply the probabilities of the two things.
step.countOutcomes: Count the favourable outcomes among the 36 possible (6 · 6).
step.complementNoSix: At least one six = 1 − the probability that neither is a six.
step.cubeVolume: The volume of a cube: side · side · side.
step.boxVolume: The volume of a box: length · width · height.
step.baseArea: Work out the area of the base – a triangle: base · height / 2.
step.prismVolume: The volume: the base area · the prism's length.
step.cylinderVolume: A cylinder's volume is π · r² · h. Do the whole numbers first: {r} · {r} · {h} = {n}.
step.coneVolume: A cone's volume is π · r² · h / 3. Do the whole numbers first: {r} · {r} · {h} = {rrh}, and divide by 3.
step.sphereVolume: A sphere's volume is 4 · π · r³ / 3. Do the whole numbers first: {r} · {r} · {r} = {rrr}, times 4, divided by 3.
step.sequenceDifference: How much do the numbers grow each time?
step.sequenceTerm: Place {n}: the first number + ({n} − 1) times the step.
step.sequenceStart: The first number, plus (n − 1) times the step {d}.
step.setEqual: Both equal y – set the expressions equal to each other.
step.insertToGetY: Put x into one of the equations.
step.addEquations: Add the equations – the y's cancel out.
trappan.prompt: Work out the division with long division.
mul.prompt: Set up the multiplication in columns and work it out.
mul.promptDecimals: Make the numbers whole, work it out – and put the decimals back at the end.
trappan.promptRest: Work out the division with long division. It doesn't go evenly – the answer is a whole number and a remainder.
trappan.promptRound: Work out the division with long division and round the answer to {n} decimals.
trappan.promptRound1: Work out the division with long division and round the answer to one decimal.
trappan.shift: You're dividing by a decimal. Move the decimal point {n} places right in both numbers – then you divide by a whole number, and the answer stays the same:
placeValue.question: What is the digit {digit} worth in the number {number}? ({place})
placeValue.hint: Check which column the digit is in - ones, tens, hundreds or thousands.
quick.mode: How do you want to answer?
ui.mirroredHint: That digit came out back to front – this is how it goes. Trace the dotted lines with your pen!
chart.question.difference: What is the difference between the number of {catA} and the number of {catB}?
chart.question.sum: How many fruits are there in total?
chart.hint.lookup: Look at the bar for {category} and read its height against the scale.
chart.hint.difference: Work out both bars' values and subtract the smaller from the larger.
chart.hint.sum: Add together the values of every bar.
statistics.question.mean: What is the mean of these numbers?
statistics.question.median: What is the median of these numbers?
statistics.question.mode: What is the mode of these numbers?
statistics.hint.mean: Add all the numbers together and divide by how many there are.
statistics.hint.median: Sort the numbers in order and find the one in the middle.
statistics.hint.mode: Count which number appears most often.
exempel.add.carry: Write the carried digit here, above.
exempel.mul.carry: Write the carried digit here, above.
exempel.sub.strike: {top} minus {bottom} doesn't work. Borrow a ten from the neighbour on the left.
exempel.sub.newValue: How many are left in that column?
exempel.sub.result: How much is left in this column?
hint.ones_over_ten: {a} + {b} = {sum}. That's {tens} ten and {ones} ones. Which digit do you write under the line?
hint.ones_over_ten_carry: {a} + {b} + {carry} (the carry) = {sum}. That's {tens} ten and {ones} ones. Which digit do you write under the line?
hint.carry_write: {a} + {b} = {sum}. That leaves {tens} ten over - write a small {tens} above the next column.
hint.forgot_carry: You forgot the carried digit! {a} + {b} + {carry} = {sum}, not just {a} + {b} = {withoutCarry}.
hint.digit_times_over_ten: {a} x {b} = {product}. That's {tens} ten and {ones} ones. Which digit do you write under the line?
hint.digit_times_over_ten_carry: {a} x {b} + {carry} (the carry) = {product}. That's {tens} ten and {ones} ones. Which digit do you write under the line?
hint.mul_carry_write: {a} x {b} = {product}. That leaves {tens} ten over - write a small {tens} above the next column.
hint.forgot_mul_carry: You forgot the carried digit! {a} x {b} + {carry} = {product}, not just {a} x {b} = {withoutCarry}.
hint.need_vaxling: {a} − {b} doesn't work, {a} is smaller than {b}. Borrow a ten from the neighbour on the left.
hint.borrow_from_zero: The zero has no tens to give. Move one more step to the left first.
hint.subtracted_smaller_from_larger: Check which digit is bigger - {b} is bigger than {a}. Work it out as 10 + {a} − {b} = {correct}.
help.note: Help is always there! The question then gives one star.
work.title: Show how you thought
work.why: Write your working here – correct working gives ★★★.
order.strokes: Write {char} like this – erase it and write it again:
order.numeratorFirst: Write the numerator first, then the fraction bar – erase and write it again.
skriv.title: Writing school
skriv.open: Writing school – learn to write digits and signs
paths.title: Training paths
paths.subtitle: Pick a path and train level by level. The same level can be on several paths – its stars come along.
paths.howReady: A level is done when you have two stars: you can do it without help. Levels that aren't open yet can be taken on as a challenge.
skriv.intro: How to write digits and signs. From year 7 the order you write in counts.
skriv.howTo: Start at 1. Follow the line and lift the pen where it ends.
skriv.order: Almost! Look at the order: start at 1 and follow the line.
skriv.unreadable: I don't see a {char} – try again, a little bigger.
step.title: Step {n}
step.howTitle: The step can look like this:
step.right: Right! Go on with the next step.
step.wrong: This step doesn't add up – check it again.
step.wrongNumber: Check {n} – where does it come from?
step.unread: I can't read the step – write it again, a little clearer.
step.more: Right so far – there are more solutions. Write them too.
step.keepGoing: Right – but not finished yet. Keep going.
step.followGuide: Right – but in Guided we take one step at a time. Do this step: {guide}
solve.mode: How do you want to write the solution?
calc.title: Work it out in a column
calc.pick: Which calculation do you want to set up?
calc.decimalsTimes: We worked it out without the decimal points: {whole}. {a} and {b} have {d} decimals together – so the answer gets {d} decimals too: {result}.
calc.decimalsPlus: The numbers were set up with {d} decimals each, decimal points under each other: {whole} becomes {result}.
calc.biggerFirst: Put the bigger number on top – swap the numbers round.
step.first: Start with the formula or the calculation, and put in the numbers from the task.
step.next: Work it out one more step.
step.signSame: Minus times minus is plus. Work out the product.
step.signDifferent: Minus times plus is minus. Work out the product.
step.minusNegative: Taking away a negative number is the same as adding. Write it as an addition.
step.plusNegative: Plus a negative number is the same as minus. Work it out.
step.powerAsProduct: Write the power as a multiplication: {b} times itself {n} times.
step.powerOfTen: Write 10 to the power of {n} as an ordinary number.
step.factorUp: The change factor for an increase of {p} %: 1 + {p} % as a decimal.
step.factorDown: The change factor for a decrease of {p} %: 1 − {p} % as a decimal.
step.groupTerms: Reorder so the x terms are together and the numbers are together.
step.combineTerms: Add up the x terms and the numbers.
step.subtractBoth: Get the x term alone: subtract {n} from both sides.
step.addBoth: Get the x term alone: add {n} to both sides.
step.collectX: Collect the x terms on the left: subtract {term} from both sides.
step.splitSquare: Write the number as {tens} {sign} {d}, in brackets, squared.
step.squareRule: Use the square rule: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².
step.findSquares: Find a and b: which squares are the first and last terms? Does the middle term match 2ab?
step.writeAsSquare: Write the expression as a bracket squared.
step.simplifyTerms: Work out and simplify each term.
step.conjugateRule: Use the conjugate rule: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².
step.findSquaresDifference: Write both terms as squares: a² − b².
step.rootBoth: Take the square root of both sides – don't forget ±.
step.bothSolutions: Write both solutions: x₁ and x₂.
step.factorOutX: Take x out as a common factor.
step.zeroProduct: A product is zero when one of its factors is zero. Write an equation for each factor.
step.pythagorasInsert: Put the legs {a} and {b} into c² = a² + b².
step.rootC: Take the square root to get c: which number times itself makes {n}? Try your way there.
step.slopeInsert: Put the points into k = Δy/Δx.
step.makeZero: Get zero on the right: move the number across.
step.pqFormula: Put p and q into the pq formula.
step.doubleRoot: The square root is 0 – there is only one solution.
step.asPowerOfTen: Write {N} as a power of ten – its lg is the exponent.
step.lgMeans: lg x = {n} means x = 10 to the power of {n}.
step.takeLg: Take lg of both sides: x = lg {N}.
step.exactValue: Use the table of exact values (or the unit circle).
step.sideFromRatio: Solve for the side: {side} = {h} times the value for the angle.
step.deriveTerms: Differentiate term by term: xⁿ becomes n·xⁿ⁻¹, bx becomes b and a constant becomes 0.
step.insertBounds: Put in the limits: F({hi}) − F({lo}).
step.pythagorasSquares: Work out the squares: {a} · {a} and {b} · {b}. Set them up in a column if you need to.
step.moveComma: You're dividing by a decimal. Move the comma {n} steps to the right in both numbers – the answer stays the same.
step.trappanDivide: Work out the division with the bus stop.
step.geo.perimeter: Go round the whole shape and add up all the sides.
step.geo.rectArea: A rectangle's area is the base times the height: {b} · {h}.
step.geo.squareArea: A square's sides are all the same. The area is side times side: {s} · {s}.
step.geo.baseTimesHeight: First the base times the height: {b} · {h}.
step.geo.parallelogram: The base times the height: {b} · {h}. The height is the dashed line – not the slanted side.
step.geo.whole: Work out the area of the whole rectangle, as if nothing were cut away: {b} · {h}.
step.geo.cutRect: Work out the area of the piece that's cut away: {b} · {h}.
step.geo.cutTriangle: The piece cut away is a triangle: {b} · {h} divided by 2.
step.geo.takeAway: Take the piece away from the whole.
step.geo.halfOfRect: The triangle is exactly half the rectangle: divide by 2.
step.geo.walls: Work out the area of the rectangle at the bottom: {b} · {h}.
step.geo.roof: The roof is a triangle: {b} · {h} divided by 2.
step.geo.radius: The radius is half the diameter: {d} / 2.
step.geo.circumferenceD: The circumference is π times the diameter: π · {d}.
step.geo.circumferenceR: The circumference is 2 · π · r. The diameter is 2 · {r} = {d}, so it's π · {d}.
step.geo.piTimes: Use π ≈ 3,14: 3,14 · {x}. Set the multiplication up in a column.
step.geo.piTimesRound: Use π ≈ 3,14: 3,14 · {x}. Set the multiplication up in a column – then round to one decimal.
step.geo.circleArea: The area is π times the radius squared. The radius squared: {r} · {r} = {rr}.
step.geo.halfCircleRadius: The half circle's diameter is the rectangle's height, {d}. The radius is half of it.
step.geo.wholeCircle: The area of a whole circle, with π ≈ 3,14: 3,14 · {r}². {r} · {r} = {rr} – then set up 3,14 · {rr}.
step.geo.halfCircle: A half circle is half the circle: divide by 2.
step.geo.holeRadius: The hole is as wide as the square: the diameter is {d}. The radius is half of it.
step.geo.takeAwayHole: Take the hole away from the square – and round to one decimal.
step.geo.ring: The ring is the big circle minus the hole. Work out R² − r² first: {R} · {R} minus {r} · {r}.
step.geo.quarterCircle: It's a quarter of a circle: divide by 4.
step.geo.areaEquation: Write the formula for the area and put in what you know. Call what you don't know h (or s).
step.geo.timesTwoBoth: Multiply both sides by 2 – that gets rid of the fraction.
step.geo.squareRoot: Which number times itself makes {area}? Try your way there: 10 · 10 = 100 helps you guess close.
step.geo.circumferenceEquation: The circumference is π · d. Write it as an equation with π ≈ 3,14.
step.geo.divideByPi: Divide both sides by 3,14. Move the comma two steps in both numbers: {c} ÷ 314 – work it out with the bus stop.
step.geo.sectorPart: How much of the circle is the sector? Simplify {v}/360 as far as it goes.
step.geo.wholeCircumference: The whole circle's circumference with π ≈ 3,14: 3,14 times the diameter {d}. Set it up in a column.
step.geo.timesParts: The sector is {p} such parts: multiply by {p}.
step.geo.divideParts: Divide by {q} with the bus stop, and round to one decimal.
step.geo.sinValue: Look up sin {C}° in the table of exact values.
step.geo.areaSine: Times the sine value, divided by 2.
step.basic.table: Think of the {b} times table and count {a} steps: {a} · {b}.
step.basic.share: Share {a} into {b} equal parts: {a} / {b}. Which number times {b} makes {a}?
step.basic.divideTable: Which number times {b} makes {a}? Think of the {b} times table.
step.basic.missingTimes: Which number times {b} makes {c}? Work out {c} / {b}.
step.basic.missingAdd: Which number plus {b} makes {c}? Count backwards: {c} − {b}.
step.basic.missingTakeAway: How much was taken from {c} to leave {a}? Work out {c} − {a}.
step.basic.missingStart: What was the number to start with? Put back what was taken away: {a} + {b}.
step.basic.clockWhole: The long hand points straight up at 12 – it's a whole hour. The short hand points at {h}.
step.basic.clockMinutes: The long hand points at {n}. Each number is 5 minutes: {n} · 5.
step.basic.clockHour: The short hand has passed {h}. It's {h} and {m} minutes: write {h}, a point, and the minutes with two digits.
step.basic.spanSameHour: From {from} to {to}: just count the minutes.
step.basic.spanToHour: From {from} to the whole hour, {hour}: 60 minus the minutes.
step.basic.spanHours: From {from} to {to} is {n} whole hours. An hour is 60 minutes.
step.basic.spanAdd: To {to} it's another {m} minutes. Add all the minutes together.
step.basic.wallet: Start with the biggest and add the smaller ones.
step.basic.howManyCoins: How many times does {coin} go into the sum? Divide by {coin}.
step.basic.count.corners: Count the corners – put a finger on each.
step.basic.count.sides: Count the sides – go round the shape.
step.basic.solid.box.corners: 4 corners on top and 4 at the bottom.
step.basic.solid.box.edges: 4 edges on top, 4 at the bottom and 4 standing up between them.
step.basic.solid.box.faces: One face on top, one at the bottom and 4 round the sides.

adv.tip.3.1.1: Minus a minus is plus. Two negative numbers multiplied make a positive.
adv.tip.3.1.2: 2⁵ means 2 · 2 · 2 · 2 · 2 – the base times itself, as many times as the exponent says.
adv.tip.3.1.3: Positive exponent: move the decimal comma right. Negative: left.
adv.tip.3.2.1: Percent means hundredths: 25 % = 0.25. Times the number gives the part.
adv.tip.3.2.2: Up by 15 % → times 1.15. Down by 20 % → times 0.80.
adv.tip.3.3.1: Add up the x terms on their own and the numbers on their own.
adv.tip.3.3.2: Do the same thing to both sides until x stands alone.
adv.tip.3.3.3: Gather all the x's on one side and the numbers on the other.
adv.tip.3.4.1: Pythagoras' theorem: c² = a² + b². Take the square root at the end.
adv.tip.3.4.2: Put the value of x into the equation. The slope k = Δy / Δx.
adv.tip.4.1.1: Write it as x² + px + q = 0 and use the pq formula.
adv.tip.4.1.2: lg x is the power 10 must be raised to, to make x: lg 1000 = 3, since 10³ = 1000.
adv.tip.4.2.1: sin v = opposite / hypotenuse, cos v = adjacent / hypotenuse. sin 30° = 0.5.
adv.tip.4.3.1: Differentiate term by term: xⁿ becomes n · xⁿ⁻¹, constants disappear.
adv.tip.4.3.2: Find an antiderivative F and work out F(b) − F(a).

geo.tip.1.2.1: The perimeter is the way all around the shape. Add up every side.
geo.tip.2.4.1: The area is base times height. A square's sides are all the same length. Perimeter: add up all four sides.
geo.tip.2.4.2: A triangle is half a rectangle: A = b · h / 2. The height is at right angles to the base.
geo.tip.2.4.3: A = b · h, where h is the height (the dashed line) – not the slanted side.
geo.tip.2.4.4: Split the shape into rectangles and triangles. Add what is there and take away what has been cut out.
geo.tip.3.4.3: d = 2r. The circumference is π · d and the area is π · r². Use π ≈ 3,14 and set the multiplication up in a column.
geo.tip.3.4.4: A = (a + b) · h / 2 – add the parallel sides, times the height, divided by two.
geo.tip.3.4.5: Work out each part on its own. A half circle is π · r² / 2. The radius is half the diameter.
geo.tip.3.4.6: Write the formula with the unknown number, put in what you know and solve for what is missing.
geo.tip.4.2.2: A sector of v degrees is v/360 of the circle – of both its area and its circumference.
geo.tip.4.2.3: T = a · b · sin C / 2, where C is the angle between the sides a and b.

adv.tip.3.3.4: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b². Don't forget the double product 2ab!
adv.tip.3.3.5: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b². Backwards: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).
adv.tip.3.3.6: x² = c has two solutions: ±√c. If x is in every term, take x out. A product is 0 when one of its factors is 0.

clock.tip.1.5.1: O'clock: the long hand points straight up at 12. Half past: it points straight down at 6 – and the short hand is halfway between two numbers.
clock.tip.1.5.3: Quarter past: the long hand at 3. Quarter to: the long hand at 9.
clock.tip.1.5.4: Each number is 5 minutes for the long hand: at 4 it's 4 · 5 = 20 minutes.
clock.tip.1.5.5: A digital clock shows hours and minutes in numbers: 7.25 is 25 minutes past 7.
clock.tip.1.5.6: After 12 the digital clock keeps counting: 13 is 1, 18 is 6. Take away 12 to get the hour on a clock with hands.
clock.tip.1.5.7: Count the fives up to the number before, then the small ticks: 4 · 5 + 3 = 23 minutes.
